keyVerseText: And it came to pass, when Jesus had ended these sayings, the people were astonished at his doctrine:
rootMeaning: The word συντελέω (synteléō) comes from the Greek components σύν (sýn), meaning 'with' or 'together,' and τελέω (teléō), meaning 'to finish' or 'complete.' This etymology highlights the idea of bringing something to completion in a cooperative or unified manner, emphasizing not just an end but a thorough and collective fulfillment. The root sense adds depth beyond the simple English glosses like 'finish' or 'end,' suggesting a process accomplished fully and in harmony with purpose or design.
usageInScripture: In Scripture, συντελέω appears seven times and is translated variously as 'had ended,' 'be fulfilled,' 'were ended,' 'ended,' 'he will finish,' and 'I will make.' This range of translations reveals that the word consistently conveys the idea of bringing something to its intended conclusion or fulfillment. Whether describing the completion of speech, events, or divine purposes, the term underscores both the finality and the accomplishment of what was intended or promised.
theologicalSignificance: Theological reflection on συντελέω reveals its profound importance in understanding God's sovereign work in history and salvation. The concept of bringing to full completion resonates with the fulfillment of God's promises and the perfect accomplishment of Christ's mission. It assures believers that God's purposes are not left unfinished but are carried out entirely and effectively. This word invites trust in the faithfulness of God to bring His redemptive plan to its consummation, encouraging perseverance and hope grounded in divine certainty.
keyVerseReflection: In Matthew 7:28, the phrase 'when Jesus had ended these sayings' uses συντελέω to indicate that Jesus fully completed His teaching at that moment. This completion marks the authoritative conclusion of His discourse, which astonished the people. The word emphasizes not just that Jesus stopped speaking, but that He brought His message to its perfect and intended close, underscoring the weight and fulfillment of His authoritative doctrine.
